issues.title: [DCN401] Cursor stutters on Xorg with two displays: static CRTC enables idle optimizations, so each cursor update does DMUB idle exit/enter
issues.author: Cláudio Forain
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

With **two displays active** on Xorg, the mouse cursor visibly speeds up and slows down while the desktop is otherwise idle. Physical mouse movement is steady, but on-screen motion is uneven. It reproduces every time and is easy to see.

* **Single display** (`xrandr --output DisplayPort-1 --off`): smooth.
* **Any rendering activity** (a tiny GL loop): smooth.
* **Kernels:** 7.1.12, 7.2.x and 7.3.3 are affected. 7.1.5 is not, because it still had [a1fc7bf6677e](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=a1fc7bf6677e) (“drm/amd/display: Restore 5s vbl offdelay for NV3x+ DGPUs”). That workaround was reverted by [f39283eab44f](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=f39283eab44f), which reached stable in 7.1.6. Older kernels (6.18.x) were also affected.
* Disabling GFXOFF, forcing `power_dpm_force_performance_level=high`, and `amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x800` (DC_DISABLE_IPS) do **not** help.

### Root cause (from ftrace + code reading)

Idle optimizations are HW-wide, but the ISM runs **per CRTC**. `dm_ism_commit_idle_optimization_state()` allows idle optimizations globally when `!vblank_enabled && dm->active_vblank_irq_count == 0`. It doesn’t check whether the **other CRTCs’ ISMs** are idle.

So the static display’s ISM reaches `OPTIMIZED_IDLE` and turns global idle on, while the cursor display is busy. Xorg’s legacy cursor moves hold no vblank reference, so nothing vetoes it.

issues.title: Idle optimizations cause stutters and freezes in Xorg
issues.author: Bruno Jacquet
issues.description:
This report is a follow-up to #4806, where it was identified that idle optimizations cause stutters and freezes on 7900x GPU.

While #4806 ended up reverting "drm/amd/display: pause the workload setting in dm" and fix stutters for most users, it is in fact not the whole story as stutters can still be seen on Xorg.

Only when idle optimizations are [completely disabled](/uploads/cae99f743e502bce18442d5789f25fec/0001-amdgpu-Never-allow-idle-optimizations.patch), then the stutters disappear for me.

To recap the reproduction scenario:
1. Simply keeping moving the cursor triggers some sporadic stutters right away where a few frames are lost (more obvious while playing a smooth video for example)
2. My best test case is: Keep pressing Alt and quickly pass over a window multiple times while clicking & dragging it away, a stutter can be felt. Then, keeping the cursor in rapid movement right after that initial stutter is often showing a complete freeze of the monitors, for as long as the cursor is being moved. It can last several seconds, and freeze stops instantly when cursor stops moving.
3. It _seems_ that some refresh rates may make the problem more or less obvious but I have no specific data on this.

My Navi 23 discrete graphics card stops working on unmodified upstream **7.4-rc1** because AMDGPU fails to initialize it during boot. AMD-Vi page faults are followed by firmware-loading errors and an AMDGPU probe failure. The card stays unbound with no render node. The integrated graphics still initialize, and the system remains accessible.

I bisected the failure to:

bf5bdfd1f8d4ad5c6020468d09b68b09c2adc5c2
iommu/amd: Force identity mode for selected GPUs only

Its exact parent is `567e74ce4dfde40a3b814de6af4adbfbe4ba1f38`.\

The fresh revert confirmation used a separate clean source worktree and an empty output directory, with no reused objects.

issues.author: Faruk Aydin

## Summary

`amdgpu_driver_release_kms()` calls `pci_set_drvdata(adev->pdev, NULL)` (drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_kms.c:1608 in v7.1.2). This function is the DRM `.release` callback, so it runs at the _final_ `drm_dev_put()` — which is deferred until the last userspace reference to the DRM device is dropped, not at unbind time.

In a GPU-passthrough workflow (unbind amdgpu -\> bind vfio-pci, standard VFIO practice), any process still holding the dGPU's DRM node open at unbind time (a GPU monitoring daemon such as LACT, a compositor, etc.) delays the final release past the point where vfio-pci has bound the device and stored its own drvdata. issues.title: RA24 little-endian is not valid for RDNA4 display hardware but is listed as supported
issues.author: fililip
issues.description:
When using KWin 6.7 (from the current KDE Plasma beta packages) on an RDNA4 dGPU, i.e. the RX 9070, the following message appears on any kind of mode programming attempt by KWin:

```
amdgpu 0000:0b:00.0: [drm] *ERROR* Unsupported screen format RA24 little-endian (0x34324152)
```

The problem is `DRM_FORMAT_RGBA8888` is listed as supported for this generation due to a common format array [here](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v7.0.10/source/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/amdgpu_dm/amdgpu_dm_plane.c#L50).

It looks like that is not the case for RDNA4, so it's probably a good idea to filter it out for this generation.

issues.title: amdgpu_vm_update_range() leaks VM-update job/IB when amdgpu_vm_ptes_update() fails; DELAYED IB pool fills, amdgpu_sa_bo_new() blocks forever (Strix Halo)
issues.author: Florin Pățan
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem


_`amdgpu_vm_update_range()`: `->prepare()` (`amdgpu_vm_sdma_prepare()`) allocates a job with a 1 KiB IB from `AMDGPU_IB_POOL_DELAYED`. If `amdgpu_vm_ptes_update()` then fails, `goto error_free` neither submits nor frees `params.job`, so the IB suballocation is never fenced and never freed.

- Each failure leaks 1 KiB of the 1 MiB pool, permanently. Leaks survive process exit.
- Once the pool is full, `amdgpu_sa_bo_new()` → `drm_suballoc_new(intr=false)` → `wait_event()` blocks forever, with no fence to wait on. The task is unkillable, its VM is never torn down, VRAM stays full, and new render-node opens fail with `-ENOMEM`. Recovery requires a reboot.
- Trigger: `-ENOMEM` from `amdgpu_vm_pt_alloc()`. On this APU, page tables are VRAM-only (`!is_app_apu`) in a 512 MiB carve-out (140 MiB of it PSP TMR).
- Any process with render-node access can trigger it.
- Mostly silent: the CS path (`amdgpu_cs_vm_handling()`) doesn't log, and `GEM_VA` logs `Couldn't update BO_VA (-12)` but returns 0.
- The same error path is in amd-staging-drm-next ba496bb.
  
  Hit in production on 7.1.13 by Vulkan (RADV) compute workloads:
- Stuck task:

issues.author: mercats
issues.description:
When a game or graphic program doesn't fully load the GPU (e.g. due to CPU/memory bottleneck or a frame rate cap) the amdgpu driver increases the core clock frequency way too much just to keep GPU load at around 70%. This results in a way higher power consumption for no increase in frame rate.

As an example with my RX 9070, the game No Rest For The Wicked capped at 110 fps uses 220 W because the driver tries to get to 70% GPU load by increasing clocks to almost 3000 MHz. Manually setting the power limit at 130 W causes the clocks to drop to 1800 MHz while the frame rate stays the same.

This happens in any game or graphic program that loads the GPU significantly but not at 100%. It's not limited to any particular game. The default GPU load targeting of 70% seems to be way too low, at least for the RX 9070 (XT). A default GPU load target of 100% probably isn't optimal for latency, but 90-95% will lower power usage a lot without increasing latency.

Edit: The GPU load target is set per profile as `PD_Data_limit_c` in `/sys/class/drm/card1/device/pp_power_profile_mode`. `BOOTUP_DEFAULT` has a value of 4587520, which is 70\*(2^16). `3D_FULL_SCREEN` has a value of 5570560, which is 85\*(2^16). And `POWER_SAVING` has a value of 5898240, which is 90\*(2^16). This corresponds exactly to the GPU load targets of 70%, 85% and 90% for the respective profiles.

With the dGPU in D3cold, attaching a USB-C dock raises GPE 0x05 and logs:

```
ACPI BIOS Error (bug): Could not resolve symbol [\_SB.PCI0.GPP0.VGA], AE_NOT_FOUND
ACPI Error: Aborting method \_GPE._L05 due to previous error (AE_NOT_FOUND)
ACPI Error: AE_NOT_FOUND, while evaluating GPE method [_L05]
```

The dGPU stays off, no hotplug reaches userspace and the external displays stay dark.

`_L05` is in the AMD CPM D3cold table (SSDT9, OEM table id `CPMD3CLD`) and is just

2. A DMI-matched GPE handler in amdgpu that replaces `_L05` when the Notify target does not

issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

On a PREEMPT_RT kernel, the system hard-locks (or panics, with panic settings enabled) when a
fullscreen game on one monitor regains focus after a window on the other monitor was active.
SubVP re-evaluation creates a phantom plane inside `dcn401_validate_bandwidth()`'s DC_FP region,
and `dc_create_plane_state()` calls `kvzalloc_obj()` there. On PREEMPT_RT the page allocator's zone
lock is a sleeping lock, so the worker sleeps while atomic. It migrates (CPU 31 → 8),
`fpu_recursion_depth` goes negative, and the later `vfree` in `dml21_destroy()` hits
`BUG_ON(in_nmi())` at mm/vmalloc.c:3428.

Three lockups on the first day of 7.3. 7.2.x ran for days on the same setup without one.

The fix is posted but unmerged: Bert Karwatzki, "drm/amd/display: fix usage of DC_FPU_{BEGIN,END}
with PREEMPT_RT" (amd-gfx, v4 2026-08-07, Fixes: 3539437f354b). I applied the equivalent locally,
plus wrapping `dc_stream_release()`/`dc_plane_state_release()` in
`dc_state_release_phantom_stream()`/`_plane()`. With that, five days, 98 h of uptime and daily
gaming sessions with the same focus switching produced no lockup and no DC_FP warning. As of
2026-10-29, `dc_create_plane_state()` is still unguarded in mainline (after the 7.4 DRM merge) and in
amd-staging-drm-next.

issues.title: drm/amdkfd: Stale KFD queues after GPU reset can trigger cascading resets
issues.author: Daniel Huang
issues.description:
## Summary

KFD queue teardown appears unable to execute during GPU reset because of a reset-domain lock conflict:

* `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()` holds `reset_domain->sem` for writing.
* `remove_queue_mes()` attempts `down_read_trylock()` on the same semaphore and immediately returns `-EIO`.
* As a result, pre-reset teardown never reaches MES. This was confirmed with kprobes across two independent hangs.

The more significant issue appears to be **incomplete post-reset queue recovery**. `kgd2kfd_post_reset()` resumes KFD without reconciling queues that could not be removed. These queues remain valid in KFD's bookkeeping but may no longer exist in firmware.

A subsequent queue operation, including implicit removal during process exit, can fail and invoke `kfd_hws_hang()`, triggering another GPU reset. In one reproduction, the GPU remained unusable until reboot.

This was discovered while investigating [ROCm/TheRock#8357](https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/8357) (gfx90c/HWS). The same locking mechanism was reproduced on gfx1103/MES.

issues.title: [Regression 7.3][DCN 3.2.1] DP 2.1 MST monitor stays black after DPMS wake: failed link training leaks MST payload slots (843049bac7 "Split DPMS ON into parts")
issues.author: darkstego
issues.description:
### Brief summary of the problem

On a DP 2.1 MST monitor, UHBR10 link training sometimes fails when the display
wakes from DPMS off. On 7.2 the driver aborts the stream enable, the MST branch
is torn down and re-detected, and the display comes back in about 4 s. On 7.3
the driver continues the enable sequence on the failed link. It allocates an MST
payload that is never released. After the topology comes back, the new payload
is written at **start slot 63** (`0x1c0 <- 01 3f 3f`) instead of 0, and the
display stays black until reboot. Replugging or power-cycling the monitor does
not recover it.

Cause: `843049bac7c0` ("drm/amd/display: Split DPMS ON into parts"). Since that
commit, `DC_DPMS_FAILED_HANDSHAKE` from `link_set_dpms_on_enable_link()` lets
`link_set_dpms_on()` continue into `link_set_dpms_on_post_enable_link()`, which
calls `allocate_mst_payload()` on the disabled link.

A one-line fix (below) restores the pre-split abort and resolves the issue here.

- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7600 (Navi 33, `1002:7480`), DCN 3.2.1, DMCUB fw `0x07003600`

issues.title: Hard lockup in dmub_srv_wait_for_idle via IPS exit from drm_vblank_enable (DCN 3.5, Strix Point)
issues.author: Alexandre DUVAL
issues.description:
## Summary

On a Strix Point (Radeon 890M, DCN 3.5) laptop, the machine hard-freezes every one
to two days. A pstore dump from one of these freezes shows a **kernel panic — Hard
LOCKUP** with the CPU stuck in `delay_halt` inside `dmub_srv_wait_for_idle()`,
reached from the IPS-exit path that `dm_read_reg_func()` triggers while reading a
display register.

The critical detail is the context: this busy-wait is entered from
`drm_vblank_get()` → `drm_vblank_enable()`, which holds `dev->vbl_lock` with
**interrupts disabled**. The register dump confirms it — `EFLAGS: 00000807`, IF
(0x200) clear. So when DMUB fails to report idle, the CPU spins forever with IRQs
off, which is why this manifests as an NMI hard lockup and a dead machine rather
than a recoverable stall or a soft lockup.

`amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x800` (`DC_DISABLE_IPS`) is an effective workaround.

- TUXEDO InfinityBook Pro AMD Gen10 (`XxKK4NAx_XxSP4NAx`)
- AMD Strix, Radeon 880M / 890M — `1002:150e` (rev c1)
- BIOS N.1.20A13, 10/14/2025
- Display: eDP-1 internal panel only, no external outputs attached

- DMUB firmware 0x09004A00 (9.0.74), loaded via PSP

## Summary

The failure is in the payload table the source writes to the hub: with `drm.debug=0x116` the DPCD `PAYLOAD_ALLOCATE_SET` (0x1c0) writes are

```
0x001c0 AUX <- (ret=  3) 01 69 12     # VCPI 1, start slot 0x69 = 105, 18 slots
0x001c0 AUX <- (ret=  3) 02 7b 1d     # VCPI 2, start slot 0x7b = 123, 29 slots
```

Start slots 105 and 123 are outside the 1..63 range of the MTP. The hub masks them to 6 bits (41 and 59), 59 + 29 overflows the table, and the resulting layout does not match the source's own stream encode

On an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, the secondary DisplayPort monitor repeatedly stops working after the session is locked and the displays have powered down due to inactivity. The primary DisplayPort monitor continues working. The secondary output disappears from KWin and is reported as **disconnected by DRM itself**. Rebooting restores both monitors, but the failure recurs, sometimes multiple times per day.

The kernel floods the journal with `gpio_service.c:315 / dal_gpio_service_open` warnings. Warnings occur in the HPD worker, PowerDevil/libddcutil's `watch_displays` thread, and `fwupd`. This is an observation, not a conclusion that either userspace service causes the failure.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: ASRock AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT / Navi 48, PCI `1002:7550` rev c0, subsystem `1849:5417`, driver `amdgpu`.
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900XT; motherboard: ASUS ROG STRIX B550-F GAMING WIFI II.
- Primary: LG Ultra HD, DP-1, 3840x2160 at 60 Hz.
- Affected secondary: Samsung U28E590, DP-2, 3840x2160 at 60 Hz, portrait rotation (90 degrees), VRR disabled in the saved KWin configuration.
- Both displays use direct DisplayPort connections, without a dock or adapter.
- Distribution: openSUSE Tumbleweed, KDE Plasma Wayland session.
- Current kernel: `7.2.11-1-default`.
- KWin: `kwin6-6.8.0-1.2`.
- PowerDevil: `powerdevil6-6.8.0-1.1`.
- libddcutil: `libddcutil5-2.2.7-1.1` (not the 3.0.0 regression).
- AMD firmware package: `kernel-firmware-amdgpu-20260926-1.1`.
- fwupd: `2.1.8-2.

issues.title: amdgpu DC: deadlock between atomic commit and hdmi_hpd_debounce_work on HDMI FRL (DCN 3.1.5 / Granite Ridge, hdmi_hpd_debounce_delay_ms=4000)
issues.author: Kiril Staikov
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem

With `amdgpu.hdmi_hpd_debounce_delay_ms=4000` and an HDMI 2.1 FRL sink, the compositor's atomic commit and amdgpu's `hdmi_hpd_debounce_work` deadlocked against each other. The compositor (Hyprland) is stuck in D state inside `drm_mode_atomic_ioctl` and never returns; the HPD IRQ worker and the FRL status poller pile up behind it. Nothing recovers; a reboot is required (and the reboot itself hangs until systemd's unit timeouts expire, because the compositor cannot be killed).

issues.title: After upgrading to 7.3.0 kscreen locker has broken colors after boot on HDR screen with color pipelines enabled
issues.author: SaberBlaze
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

I use KDE on Arch Linux with auto login, screen lock after login and `KWIN_DRM_USE_COLOR_PIPELINE=1`. After the boot my screen locker on HDR screen has weird colors. After unlocking session colors are becoming normal, and all subsequent screen locks have normal colors as well. This is a regression in kernel 7.3.0.

## Hardware description:
 - CPU: 9800X3D
 - GPU: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. [AMD/ATI] Navi 48 [Radeon RX 9070/9070 XT/9070 GRE] [1002:7550] (rev c0)
 - System Memory: 64 GiB
 - Display(s): 2K SDR VRR, 4K HDR VRR, 1080p SDR 60Hz
 - Type of Display Connection: DP, DP, DP

## System information:
 - Distro name and Version: Arch Linux
 - Kernel version: 7.3.0
 - Custom kernel: cachyos
 - AMD official driver version: mesa 3:26.2.5-1

## How to reproduce the issue:

1. Enable HDR on one of the monitors
2. Put `KWIN_DRM_USE_COLOR_PIPELINE=1` into your environment file to enable color pipelines: https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kwin/-/wikis/Environment-Variables#usage
3. In KDE, enable autologin and automatic screen lock after login: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/KDE#Lock_screen
4. Reboot
5. After the boot, you'll be automatically login in your accout, yet kscreen locker will engage and it will have broken colors.
